topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: The space where the tree once stood is now a patch of sunlight, a gap through which the sky peers into the yard, uninvited. I remember the day my hands, small and awkward, buried the sapling in the soil, the way the earth crumbled and stuck to my nails, a promise sealed in dirt. Now, the stake that once supported it stands alone, a silent witness to the change. The grass around it is neatly trimmed, as if nothing ever rooted here deeper than dandelions. I trace the outline of where the trunk should be, my fingers searching for what isn’t there, finding only air.
